country: Europe (European Association of Urology YAU group)
models_evaluated: 4 AI platforms (others not named in abstract)

links.outcome: AI chatbot scores on textbook MCQs versus urology experts; exam-style benchmark used
links.effect: Mean AI score 15/31 vs experts 14/31 (P=0.802); ChatGPT-4 24/31. Authors state use alone is unsuitable for clinical reasoning and needs validation on real clinical cases.
links.quote: These findings support a potential role for AI in educational settings and for answering well-defined theoretical questions, but their use alone is not suitable for clinical reasoning.

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance on multiple-choice questions from a urology review book compared to human experts without testing deployment practices or safeguards.
